titleStmt.author: Publius Ovidius Naso

respStmt.resp: Independent second manuscript-image reading of all 70 verses and adjudication of every first-pass note
respStmt.name: OpenAI Codex, independent encode_s agent

publicationStmt.p: Amores Project working transcription, 9 September 2026. Independently reviewed by a second agent; not human-approved.

handDesc.handNote: Brown main writing and darker interventions are visible. Ink differences are recorded without assigning historical hands.

origin.p: The supplied library manifest dates the manuscript to the 10th/11th century; this does not date individual interventions.

surrogates.p: Library digital facsimile, PPN1844735508. The supplied manifest identifies the images as Public Domain Mark 1.0. Every verse in folios 58r, 58v, 59r was inspected for this first pass.

projectDesc.p: Source-grounded transcription of all 70 manuscript verses followed by an independent second image pass. No other witness or normalized edition was used as transcription input. Existing annotation coordinates provide navigation, not text. Duplicate annotation records were identical in page and rectangle; one record per verse was reused without changing annotations.

correction.p: Uncertain letters are marked unclear and unreadable text gap. Darker ink is hi, not proof of erasure or a distinct hand. Actual additions use add; deletion or substitution is asserted only with visible evidence and qualified where needed. No unattested earlier reading is supplied.

normalization.p: Single source-oriented display. Ordinary allographs and long s are represented with standard Latin characters. Source spelling, including e caudata as ę, is preserved; word spacing and couplet layout are editorial. Explicit abbreviation expansions remain in TEI choices. Punctuation and unusual signs are schematic typographic equivalents, not exact pen-shape replicas.

punctuation.p: Visible significant punctuation and separation or insertion marks are retained. No modern sentence punctuation is supplied.

segmentation.p: Each l is one verse and one physical source line. Even lines are indented; lg groups are editorial elegiac couplets. Each verse has a stable ID and an existing facsimile rectangle. The rectangles may include neighbouring text and need not enclose marginal inscriptions.

interpretation.p: Every note has been independently investigated. Observations record supported readings and features; uncertainties retain image or interpretation limits without asserting an unsupported earlier state or normalized correction. The accompanying second-pass ledger records all dispositions. No consequential editorial decision remains for escalation.

revisionDesc.change: First source pass covering all 70 verses and visible interventions in folios 58r, 58v, 59r; awaiting a different agent's independent reading.

Independently inspected all 70 verses and all 36 first-pass notes against folios 58r–59r. Corrected supported transcription errors and source spellings, retained ambiguous strokes without unsupported expansions, and documented uncertain interventions without inventing replacement readings.
Reinspected verse 67 and its source graphic; added a corrected candidate TEI zone and linked the verse to it, retaining the supplied erroneous zone for provenance without changing annotation data.

lg.l: Stat uetus &et multos incaedua silua per annos
Credibile est illi numen inesse loco
Fons sacer in medio speluncaque pumice pendens
Et latere ex omni dulce queruntur aues
Hic ego dum spacior tectus nemoralibus umbris
Quod mea quaerebam musa mouer&et opus·
Venit odoratos elegia nexa capillos
Et puto pes illi longior alter erat·
Forma decens uestis tenuissima uultus amantis
Et pedibus uitium causa decoris erat·
Venit &et ingenti uiolenta tragoedia passu
Fronte comę torua palla iacebat humi·
Laeua manus sceptrum late regale mouebat
Lydius alpta pedum uincla coturnus erat·
Et prior &et quis erit dixit tibi finis amandi ⸮
O argumenti lente poeta tui ⸮
Nequitiam uinosa tuam conuiuia narrant
Narrant in multas conpita secta uias·
Saepe aliquis digito uatem designat euntem
Atque ait hic hic est quem ferus urit amor·
Fabula nec sentis tota iactaris in urbe
Dum tua praeterito facta pudore refers·
Tempus erat thyrso pulsū grauiore moueri
Cessatum satis est· incipe maius opus·
Materia premis ingenium· cane facta uirorum
Haec animo dices area dignafacta meo est
Quod tenerę cantent lusit tua musa puellę
Primaque per numeros acta iuuenta suos·
Nunc habeam per te romana tragoedia nomen
Inplebit leges spiritus isteipse meas·
Hactenus &et mouit pictis innexa coturnis
Densum caesarie terque quaterque capud·
Altera si memini limis subrisit ocellis
Fallor an indecora myrtea uirga fuit
Quid grauibus uerbis animosa tragoedia dixit
Me premis an numquam non grauis esse potes ⸮
Imparibus tamen est numeris dignata moueri
In me pugnasti uersibus usa meis·
Non ego contulerim sublimia carmina nrīsnostris
Obruit exiguas regia uestra fores·
Sum leuis &et mecum leuis est mea cura cupido
Non sum materia fortior ipsa mea·
Rustica est sine me lasciui mater amoris
Huic ego proueni lena comesque deae·
Quam tū non poteris duro reserare coturno
Haec est blanditiis ianua laxa meis·
Et tamen emerui plusquam tu posse ferendo
Multa super cilio non patienda tuo·
Per me decepto didicit custode corinna
Liminis adstrictę sollicitare fidem fores
Delabique toro tunica uelata soluta
Atque inpercussos nocte mouere pedes·
Vel quotiens foribus duris incisa pependi
Non uerita a populo praetereunte legi·
Quin ego me memini dum custos saeuus abir&et
Ancillę missam delituisse sinu·
Quid cum me munus natali mittis ad tilla
Rumpta &et adpositam barbara mersit aqua
Prima tuae moui felicia semina mentis
Munus habes&et quod te iam petit ista meum
Desierat coepi per uos utramque rogamus
In uacuas aures uerba timentis eant·
Altera me sceptro decoras altoque coturno·
Iam nunc contracto magnus in ore sonus orbe sonor
Altera das nostrom uicturum nomen amoris
Exioga des &et longis uersibus adde breues
Exiguum uati concede tragoedia tempus·
Tu labor aeternus quod petit illa breue est·
Mota dedit ueniam· teneri properentur amores
Dum uacat a tergo grandius urg&et opus·

div.head: First-pass source notes
div.note: The large S begins the poem beneath a book-transition rubric. Uetus is darker and its final s has a raised curled form. A hole between per and annos does not demonstrably remove verse letters; no textual gap is invented. The rubric belongs to the book transition and is described here rather than inserted into verse 1.
The area after omni is faint or disturbed. No readable deleted letters are established; the visible line continues dulce queruntur aues.
The et ligature completing moueret is darker. It is preserved as a glyph with explicit expansion, as are comparable et signs elsewhere.
The initial o of odoratos is visibly darker. No earlier character is reconstructed.
Tragoedia is retained from the visible sequence; a darker or crowded beginning does not establish an erased predecessor.

A small p-like character stands above alta, approximately over the l/t boundary. Its precise reading, anchor and function are uncertain; the visible above-line material is retained without forcing a grammatical expansion.
Question-like signs follow amandi and tui in 15–16. Their display is schematic, and the stops are not modern punctuation supplied from another text.
The n of uinosa is darker. The witness reading is retained without a reconstructed earlier state.
The sequence is iactaris; the high initial i-like stroke is treated as an ordinary allograph, not a separate addition.

The y-like character in thyrso is faint. The visible marked form pulsū is retained without an expansion: the horizontal stroke is clear, but its function does not securely establish a nasal or an unmarked pulsu reading.
The initial M is disturbed but the word Materia remains legible. No earlier reading is supplied.
Digna is legible above baseline facta. No unambiguous deletion is visible; the addition and baseline word are retained separately, without asserting a replacement relationship.
Habeam includes a fine dark stroke within the word. It is retained without asserting that the stroke cancels a particular letter.
Independent enlargement supports the above-line word iste. Baseline ipse has no assured cancellation, so both are retained and their possible replacement relationship remains unspecified.
The m of mouit is darker. The remaining visible sequence reads pictis innexa coturnis.
The witness spelling capud is visible, with a tall final d; no silent change to caput is made.
Si and the end of ocellis are darker. The area before memini is disturbed; no underlying words or historical correcting hand are inferred.
The m of myrtea is darker. The source spelling is retained.
Independent enlargement confirms the barred contraction represented schematically as nrīs, expanded nostris. The typography is not an exact replica of the manuscript bar placement.
The it of Obruit is darker. Adjacent faint traces do not justify reconstructing erased letters.
The end of leuis is darker. A hole in the adjacent space does not establish missing text; the et sign is separately encoded.
The visible marked form tū carries a horizontal stroke. Its function remains uncertain, so no tu or tum expansion is imposed; the literal marked form is retained.
The m of meis is darker; the current text and source spacing are retained with editorial segmentation.

The source writes adstrictę with e caudata. Baseline fidem and darker marginal fores are both legible. No secure cancellation or linking sign establishes replacement; the marginal word is retained without assigning that relationship.
The opening quotiens and the following line’s uerita are on disturbed areas. The words remain legible; no earlier text is reconstructed.
The final et sign in abiret is retained with a declared expansion. The note is distinct from the manuscript line, not extra verse text.

A small t-like addition appears above the area between ad and illa. Its anchoring and role are uncertain. The baseline sequence is preserved without silently changing it to an expected illa or illi construction.

The word beginning Ru is disturbed; an m-like trace before pta remains under unclear, without an inferred deletion action. Independent reinspection confirms final aqua, without a following m; the first-pass aquam has been corrected.
The area in tuae is disturbed but the current reading is retained. Prima tuae moui is transcribed from the image.

Independent inspection restores the clearly written te after quod. Small es stands above the baseline et sign in habet. No secure deletion of that sign establishes a substitution; both visible inscriptions are retained without an expanded corrected reading.
Coepi is faint in the disturbed left portion. The remainder reads per uos utramque rogamus; it is not normalized to an expected verb ending.
The e of me and initial s of sceptro are darker. Sceptro is a baseline word, not a marginal addition.

A small r-like character stands above contacto; darker right annotation orbe sonor is legible. Baseline in ore sonus remains visible. The uncertain character and unspecified relationships are preserved without forcing substitution.
The o in nostrom is darker and a horizontal stroke crosses the following m-like form. A qualified deletion records the visible stroke; no replacement vowel or earlier word is invented.

The baseline opening appears Exiga des. Independent enlargement reads the above-line loop as o; its anchoring and role remain tentative. The visible forms are retained without supplying a normalized word.
The u in uacat and final et sign in urget are darker. The next poem begins below this verse and is not part of 3.1.
Independent reinspection reads comę and palla. The first pass expanded the e caudata and inserted an unsupported i in palla; both have been corrected.
The source writes e caudata in tenerę and puellę. These letter forms are retained rather than silently expanded to ae.
The source reads Ancillę missam: e caudata and missam are retained from the visible letters.
Independent inspection confirms Mota, with the crossbar of t visible. The first-pass Mora has been corrected.

The supplied annotation rectangle points to the next poem opening. Independent reinspection verifies this verse on the first text line of folio 59r and establishes a corrected TEI zone (125,265)–(1530,370), now linked from this verse. Original zone (103,536)–(1460,622) is preserved as provenance; annotations.json is unchanged.
